races.name: ITBA Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Bayonetta
runners_data.note: Experienced eight-year-old with a consistent prominent style who handles good ground (12/15 sim-going record) and trips around 2m, tongue tie fitted, seven pounds claimer Kevin Healy takes the ride for a trainer who has just one run from 14-day runners.

runners_data.name: Cool Native
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy booked for this six-year-old trained by Gordon Elliott, whose T14 strike-rate of 10/63 is active; returning from 93 days off, course form sparse but prior win on good shows the ground is suitable.

runners_data.name: Fastnet Crystal
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien sends this five-year-old back after 183 days off; carries a high STYLE_FIT flag indicating she is moving from her natural prominent role to a lead role, so her chance of dominating is tempered — she may be outrun if the race quickens sharply.

runners_data.name: Hello Below
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old for Colin Bowe, whose trainer has 1/1 in the 14-day window; unrated style sits as unknown, and the single piece of good-ground form (6th over 22f) leaves questions; bear in mind before backing.

runners_data.name: Jet To Glory
runners_data.note: John McConnell runner whose trainer shows 0/48 in the 14-day column — a cold stat; form reads P2-545 with three recent runs all on good ground suggesting no going concern, though the horse has yet to win in this type.

runners_data.name: Jolly D'olivate
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for P J Rothwell returning from 86 days off, going rated unknown and style listed as unknown; form string includes falls and pulled-ups (/1FPP-), which makes jumping reliability the key question here.

runners_data.name: Mercurial Sea
runners_data.note: Paddy Cleary (7lb claimer) takes over for Nigel Slevin, whose stable shows 0/0 in the 14-day column; the horse has placed three times over hurdles and handles good ground, sitting just off prominent pace, though a rating of 88 is the lowest in this field.

runners_data.name: Nelliestar
runners_data.note: Hold-up type flagged for fading in finishes; all recent form history shows double-digit finishes at shorter trips on standard ground, so this step up in trip at this level looks very ambitious for Thomas Patrick McGettigan's mare.

runners_data.name: Room For One More
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins sends this five-year-old out for just its second run after 133 days off; lightly raced with a single start (6th on soft), the hold-up style and powerful stable backing make it one to treat with respect despite thin form.

runners_data.name: Three Leaf Clover
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner flagged for fading, and the form string of 000 confirms that pattern; Dermot McLoughlin's five-year-old has shown nothing in three starts and returns after 119 days, making it very hard to make a case.

runners_data.name: My Girl Rosie
runners_data.note: Four-year-old filly carrying a fade flag; both runs have been at 2m on good ground with finishes of 8th and 9th, so she is yet to show anything meaningful, and at the minimum age in this field she faces a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Ritz Plan
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type for S R B Crawford — four runs all placed (242-4) and handles varying ground well; the step up to 2m2f is the key query, but J J Slevin takes the ride and the horse has never run worse than fourth.

races.paceDynamic: Fastnet Crystal is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 12-runner maiden hurdle over 2m2f on good ground, and with no other horse carrying a Lead style, she is set to control proceedings from the front unchallenged. The prominent types — Bayonetta, Cool Native, Mercurial Sea, and Ritz Plan — will likely settle just behind her, creating an organised pace with a single horse on the engine rather than a contested lead. Given the absence of pace pressure, Fastnet Crystal can dictate a measured tempo, which will compress the race into the final climb and reward those who travel well through it rather than those who need a strong gallop to reel in leaders. This shape firmly favours well-travelling prominent racers and hold-up horses with the class to pick off a steady-paced leader in the straight, with Cool Native and Room For One More the profile types best placed to exploit a controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fastnet Crystal controls unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Fastnet Crystal settles in front at a fair-to-slow clip and the race bunches behind her until the last.
scenarios.body: Fastnet Crystal sets every fraction she chooses, and the race becomes a test of jumping fluency and a late sprint rather than stamina; hold-up horses and prominent types with a strong finishing kick are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent racer presses home
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent horses tracks Fastnet Crystal closely enough to wear her down and strikes from the front turning in.
scenarios.body: Bayonetta or Ritz Plan, racing in the first two or three throughout, lands upsides approaching the last and the extra experience or class advantage decides it on the run-in; a horse happy to be delivered close to the pace benefits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely steady and a well-bred hold-up type finds clear running off the home turn to pick off the tired leaders.
scenarios.body: Room For One More, carrying Mullins connections and lightly raced profile, is the type who could cruise through a slowly run race and arrive late with a decisive challenge; Jet To Glory, coming from off the pace, also fits if she travels well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse and attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors disrupt the field order and several prominent horses fade, gifting an uncontested win to a surprise stayer.
scenarios.body: A loose, fractured race in which jumping becomes the decisive factor rather than tactical positioning; a horse jumping fluently throughout lands in front by default.

watchPoints.text: Fastnet Crystal's STYLE_FIT flag means she is racing outside her natural role as a prominent horse — watch whether she actually bowls off in front or drifts back, as her position in the early stages will shape the entire race.
Cool Native returns from 93 days off for Gordon Elliott with Jack Kennedy, a significant jockey booking — watch the market move for signs this layoff is hiding a better-than-usual preparation.
Jolly D'olivate has fallen and pulled up in recent starts; a jumping blunder early from this horse could cause interference for the closely-packed prominent group chasing Fastnet Crystal.

Room For One More (Mullins/O'Keeffe) is essentially a debut-in-hurdling unknown over this trip — watch how she travels through the race from the hold-up position, as a smooth passage would signal a dangerous late run.

Ritz Plan has placed four times without winning; watch whether J J Slevin opts to press Fastnet Crystal from flag-fall, as any move to share the lead would turn a solo-run scenario into a genuine pace duel.

races.name: Randox (C & G) Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Liceo
runners_data.note: Tipped headgear (tp) and has placed at this sort of trip on good ground, but his natural hold-up style is compromised here — with multiple hold-up horses in the field, he is unlikely to get a clean rails run from the back and may end up racing closer than ideal, dulling his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Your Call
runners_data.note: 107 days off the track and no wins from 6 starts, with his best efforts coming in held-up roles on good ground; the long absence combined with being shuffled away from his preferred position at the rear makes it hard to fancy him finding improvement.

runners_data.name: Fortis Et Liber
runners_data.note: Completely unknown quantity for Colin Bowe, who sends a runner in for a trainer who struck on his sole runner in the last 14 days — no form to dissect but the freshness and stable confidence give him each-way intrigue.

runners_data.name: Fuusland
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's yard is firing (10/63 in 14 days) and this horse ran on good ground last time, but a 'U' result over 20f suggests jumping reliability is a live question on his debut for the stable — market support will be telling.

runners_data.name: G N Jefferson
runners_data.note: Flags a tendency to fade in the closing stages, and with 60 days between runs and only one relevant run on similar going, he is likely to be outpaced late in what looks a race where the tempo is not strong enough to set up a grind.

runners_data.name: Jet Renegade
runners_data.note: Most consistent of the genuine hold-up horses with a third from five starts and solid recent form at longer trips on good ground; best served by a stronger pace than this race is likely to produce, but his jumping experience gives him claims.

runners_data.name: Luker's Tipple
runners_data.note: The one horse who can genuinely pressure Direct Approach up front for Gavin Cromwell and Keith Donoghue — six placed efforts from recent starts and a fine record at 16f on good ground make him the most obvious threat to the leader if he sits second and pings the last.

runners_data.name: Direct Approach
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott on this front-running type returning from 195 days off; if his jumping holds up on only his second hurdles start, the combination of uncontested lead and top jockey/trainer pairing makes him the dominant tactical force in this race, though the long layoff is a real caveat.

runners_data.name: Mytommy
runners_data.note: Only run shows an eighth of eight on soft ground; stepping up in trip and switching to good ground for J J Slevin, but the bare form gives nothing to work with and a tendency to fade late would be a concern in a race where the leaders are unlikely to come back to him.

races.paceDynamic: Direct Approach is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Jack Kennedy in the saddle for Gordon Elliott, is likely to set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without any serious pressure from the remainder of the field. Luker's Tipple is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely sit second or just off Direct Approach's shoulder, meaning the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to burn off those tracking close. The hold-up brigade — G N Jefferson, Jet Renegade, Mytommy, Liceo, and Your Call — will be operating from further back, and with only one genuine pace-setter, the tempo is unlikely to be severe enough to bring them into the race late. This race shape — a single uncontested front-runner setting a modest gallop — strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce from a close-up position, rather than horses needing a strong pace to reel leaders in; the field holds more hold-up types than the rear positions can accommodate, and Liceo and Your Call, true hold-up horses by nature, are the most likely to be denied their natural position and forced to race out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Direct Approach Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Direct Approach dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the hold-up horses cannot generate enough momentum from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Direct Approach sets fractions that suit himself and Luker's Tipple, who tracks throughout and is best placed to challenge at the last; with no rival to press the front-runner, those from the rear lack the late injection of pace needed to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Luker's Tipple pushes Direct Approach for the lead, creating a genuine two-horse battle that opens the door for a closer.
scenarios.body: A contested front sets a stronger gallop than expected, weakening both lead horses in the closing stages; a horse tracking just off them — ideally one with decent form at this trip — picks up the pieces.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Type Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced, unexposed horses — Fortis Et Liber or Fuusland — proves significantly better than their bare form and travels powerfully into contention.
scenarios.body: Gordon Elliott's Fuusland has form over course-relevant good ground and a powerful stable behind it, while Fortis Et Liber is completely unexposed for Colin Bowe; either could bolt up if their unknown ceiling is high.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the front two tire significantly inside the final flight, allowing the hold-up horses to come home late.
scenarios.body: Liceo and Your Call are the likeliest beneficiaries on paper but are racing out of their natural hold-up role having been pushed forward by the field shape, reducing the probability this materialises; Jet Renegade is the most genuine closer in this group.

watchPoints.text: Direct Approach's jumping — on just his second hurdles start after 195 days off, any blunder at a flight could end his advantage immediately and completely reshape the race.
Fuusland unseated on his sole start; monitor his jumping in the early stages as another jumping incident would confirm he is not yet reliable enough to factor.

If Luker's Tipple pushes forward aggressively from the flag and contests the lead with Direct Approach, the resulting stronger pace would significantly increase the chance for hold-up horses like Jet Renegade to come with a late run.

Liceo and Your Call — both natural hold-up horses — should be watched leaving the stalls to see how far forward they end up; if either is forced wide or unusually close, their finishing effectiveness will be materially reduced.

Fortis Et Liber runs with no public form; watch the market in the final 20 minutes before post time as any significant stable-backed move would suggest Colin Bowe holds the horse in unusually high regard.

races.name: Join Racing TV Now With A Free Trial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on Good ground and has solid course-distance form (14/15 runs on similar going); hold-up style suits a competitive race where Bryson has set an honest pace, and the 7lb claim for Caragh Monaghan could be a factor off OR 100.

runners_data.name: Bryson
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here but racing out of his natural hold-up role — expect him to be placed positively by Sam Ewing, though his OR 97 mark and form line showing a fall and unseating (0B6-U2) adds jumping risk at the head of affairs.

runners_data.name: Broken Ice
runners_data.note: A consistent prominent-style racer with four places in his last five and proven on Good turf; at 10 years old stamina is confirmed, and Alex Harvey keeps this veteran competitive off OR 96 — ideally positioned if Bryson's pace is sustainable.

runners_data.name: Small Bucks
runners_data.note: Holds-up but fades in the finish — that combination in an 18-runner handicap off OR 94 is limiting; the conditional jockey ride and a form line showing a pull-up and a 13th suggest confidence should be modest.

runners_data.name: My Mate Tony
runners_data.note: True hold-up type who typically races at the rear but the crowded field means securing a natural position will be difficult; fades in finish is a noted flag, and five consecutive double-figure finishes on Good ground make this hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Sneddy Eddie
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse trained by Gordon Elliott with Jack Kennedy booked — that combination always commands respect — but his form on Good ground (0W0P in six similar-ground starts) and recent finishes of 13th and 26th make the booking more attractive than the form.

runners_data.name: Turkey And Ham
runners_data.note: Has a win and a place on Good ground and showed he can race prominently in practice; placed in good company at Downpatrick's trip before, and Simon Torrens is a capable pilot — likely to push forward from his hold-up base in this large field.

runners_data.name: Trixaboutmaisie
runners_data.note: Off 261 days, fades in the finish, and all three career runs on Good ground have yielded no win or place; the Bowe yard has had rare runners lately (T14: 1/1) and the long layoff makes this a significant risk.

runners_data.name: Centaq
runners_data.note: Has been placed twice from 13 runs on Good ground and races prominently; Alix Balfe (7lb claimer) aboard and the OR 82 mark gives a weight advantage — has the profile to sit just behind Bryson and capitalise if the pace is steady.

runners_data.name: Firstupbestdressed
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who has proven Good-ground form (6/7 runs in similar conditions showing places); off 66 days and a career without a win, but Philip Donovan gives this veteran a chance in a big-field handicap where traffic can be navigated.

runners_data.name: Gortmore Lady
runners_data.note: Trainer Ciaran Murphy has had 2 winners from 13 in 14 days (active yard); Gortmore Lady's natural hold-up style is disrupted by the large field, and her OR 80 and recent fall (B) on her last run tempers enthusiasm despite the in-form trainer angle.

runners_data.name: Volez Vous
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish, has been pulled up in three of five recent starts, and the Good-ground record (1W from 7 similar runs) is limited; the hold-up style mapped to midfield due to field congestion further reduces the probability of a clean run.

runners_data.name: Glenriver
runners_data.note: Off 156 days and a career form of P/PPP — consecutive pulled-ups is a serious concern; a hold-up type in a competitive 18-runner field who fades in the finish and returns from a long break is likely to be making up the numbers.

runners_data.name: Stormy Jenn
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up horse off OR 77 with one career place and a fall on last run (F); the 45-day break and Josh Williamson (5) conditional booking does not inspire confidence in a race this competitive.

runners_data.name: Kalsman
runners_data.note: Has two wins and three places from 10 runs on Good ground — the best similar-going record of any hold-up horse in the field; off OR 99, the Reserve 1 jockey booking is the only caveat, but if a confirmed jockey takes the ride this profile looks underrated.

runners_data.name: King Of The Greys
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish, is a natural hold-up horse, and four consecutive double-figure finishes including a pulled-up; OR 100 is the joint top weight and Reserve 2 is not an inspiring booking — profile does not suit this race shape.

runners_data.name: Pahlavi
runners_data.note: Ran just 2 days ago — the shortest last-run interval in the field — which is a significant fitness flag even if John Joseph Hanlon is a confident trainer (1 winner/34 in 14 days); the Reserve 3 jockey and 9-year-old age make this a difficult proposition on quick turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Bryson is the one confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner handicap hurdle and, racing out of his natural hold-up role, is expected to slot in at the head of affairs and control tempo at Downpatrick's 2m2f trip on Good ground. With no other genuine pace horse to challenge him, Bryson should dictate a sustainable, measured gallop rather than a frantically contested lead — the kind of rhythm that keeps the field bunched and largely in contention entering the home straight. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types: Sneddy Eddie, Turkey And Ham, My Mate Tony, Trixaboutmaisie, Gortmore Lady, Volez Vous and several others are genuine closers redistributed into midfield slots on the map because there are far more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — of those, Sneddy Eddie (Kennedy/Elliott) and Turkey And Ham are most likely to press nearest to the pace in reality. A controlled, single-paced lead with a chasing pack throughout strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off Bryson and pick him up in the straight, making the two or three horses capable of racing in a genuine tracking position — close enough to the leader without burning fuel — the primary tactical beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bryson Controls, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Bryson sets a fair, uncontested pace and horses positioned just behind him through the race travel comfortably into the home straight.
scenarios.body: Bryson's controlled front-running compresses the field, and horses who track him in second or third position get first run at the final hurdles with the advantage of a clear passage; the sustainable tempo means they arrive fresh enough to assert.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Contested Mid-Race, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If several redistributed hold-up types push forward early and create more pace than expected, stringing the field out.
scenarios.body: A quicker mid-race tempo burns off horses who have overcommitted to prominent positions, leaving the race open for those who have genuinely held up and produced a late charge; Sea Of Doubt and Kalsman, both proven in similar good-ground conditions, are best positioned to exploit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Bryson is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged and the pace is so modest that his rivals can never close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: An unchallenged Bryson sets a dawdle-then-sprint scenario that plays to his natural jumping fluency, and the bunched finish paradoxically rewards the horse furthest forward because late runners are caught in traffic; Centaq's prominent racing style and course-distance profile makes him a danger.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Test, Held-Up Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the going plays slower than the unknown going report suggests and jumping errors thin the field in the latter stages.
scenarios.body: A grinding, attrition-style finish nullifies hold-up types who race wide or lose position but rewards those with proven stamina at the trip and sound jumping; Turkey And Ham's track-form on good ground and Kalsman's course-distance wins give them genuine claims in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Kalsman's similar-going record (2W3P from 10 runs on Good ground) is the standout hold-up horse statistic in this race — watch whether the Reserve 1 jockey booking is confirmed before the off, as a named rider significantly upgrades this runner's claims.

Bryson is the lone front-runner racing out of his natural role — watch his jumping from the front, as his form contains a fall and unseated (0B6-U2) and a jumping error at the head of an 18-runner field could bring down multiple horses.

Turkey And Ham and Sneddy Eddie (Kennedy/Elliott) are both likely to push forward from their mapped midfield positions, potentially crowding Bryson's pace earlier than expected and creating a more contested early tempo than the single pace-setter scenario suggests.

Pahlavi ran only 2 days ago — monitor the going report update for Downpatrick, as an unknown surface combined with a 2-day turnaround on a 9-year-old is a significant welfare and performance risk in a 18-runner jumping contest.

With 18 runners over 2m2f at Downpatrick, track position at the first flight will be critical — horses drawn wide in the stalls or slow to load face a significant early disadvantage in securing their natural racing position, particularly for those true hold-up types mapped to midfield.

races.name: Plus 2 Print Remembering Tony Oakes MBE Maiden Hurdle
Go fibrefast With Fibrus Broadband Rated Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Playtime
runners_data.note: Prominent racer carrying Gordon Elliott's leading jockey Jack Kennedy, consistent in similar good ground over this sort of trip with three place efforts from four recent runs, and should get the ideal pitch just off Lemmy Caution's shoulder — the most natural heir if the favourite weakens.

runners_data.name: Lemmy Caution
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning from 48 days off with strong course form at 2m4f, wears a hood, and has course-distance form to back up its pace role; the uncontested lead in a six-runner novice hurdle is a significant tactical gift, though the layoff is worth monitoring late in the race.

runners_data.name: Surfin Usa
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained and a genuine pace horse by nature, but with Lemmy Caution and Playtime likely to fill the early positions, it will be forced to race further off the pace than it prefers — that positional compromise makes its 1W1P similar-going record harder to convert, even if the raw ability is there.

runners_data.name: Butch Coolidge
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a patchy record — five of six recent runs have yielded finishes outside the frame on good ground — but owns a win at 2m6f on good ground which shows the trip and conditions aren't a concern; needs a troubled pace to bring late runners into play.

runners_data.name: Gangster Granny
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with two wins at 2m6f on good ground and a solid recent placed effort, giving it the best profile of the rear-division runners if the race develops into a test of stamina; trainer C A McBratney has a quiet 14-day strike rate but Darragh O'Keeffe is a shrewd pilot in these situations.

runners_data.name: Written In My Soul
runners_data.note: Recent form is deeply concerning — two pulled-up efforts among the last three runs, and the history at this distance on good ground shows no wins or places from nine attempts; redistributed from a true hold-up role because the map is crowded at the rear, but the form makes meaningful involvement very unlikely regardless of race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Lemmy Caution is the confirmed front-runner here and, in a six-runner field, should be able to control proceedings from the front without meaningful pressure — the pace will be sustainable rather than searingly honest, set to suit a horse that wants to dictate and conserve energy over 2m6f of hurdles. Playtime is the only natural rival for a prominent pitch, likely to track Lemmy Caution in second, which means this shapes as a two-horse front group with the remainder strung out behind. This field actually holds more genuine prominent/pace-inclined horses than can occupy that ground: Surfin Usa is a natural front-runner but is mapped to midfield because Lemmy Caution and Playtime are likely to claim the front positions first, so Surfin Usa will race further back than it wants to. The resulting shape — a controlled, low-tempo lead set by a fresh and confident front-runner — strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the pace and deliver their effort off a steady gallop, rather than hold-up types asked to produce a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lemmy Caution Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Lemmy Caution dictates an uncontested lead and the pace remains steady throughout.
scenarios.body: Lemmy Caution, fresh off a 48-day break and with the confidence of recent course form, sets a measured gallop that nullifies late runners and rewards those who travel close to the pace; Playtime, tracking throughout under Jack Kennedy, is the most obvious beneficiary if Lemmy Caution weakens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Lemmy Caution sets a fair gallop but is run down inside the final two flights by a horse that has tracked throughout.
scenarios.body: Playtime, with strong Gordon Elliott booking and solid form in similar going, tracks the pace perfectly and produces a straightforward challenge; Surfin Usa, despite being pushed back from its natural pitch, could still get competitive if it travels smoothly into contention from the reshaped midfield position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the final mile and sets up a late finishing burst.
scenarios.body: Gangster Granny has two wins at 2m6f on good ground and a genuine hold-up profile, making it the most credible finisher if the race falls apart; Butch Coolidge stays on late but has struggled for consistency and would need everything to go right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If a falter, unseating, or series of jumping errors scrambles the race order completely.
scenarios.body: Written In My Soul's dismal recent form — five runs producing two pulled-up performances — makes it unlikely to benefit even in a chaotic race; Butch Coolidge, who recorded a win at 2m6f on good ground, is the most likely beneficiary of a race that falls apart in front of it.

watchPoints.text: Lemmy Caution's 48-day layoff — watch how sharp it is at the early hurdles; any jumping errors under a fresh horse could unsettle a seemingly straightforward front-running plan.

Surfin Usa will be fighting for a position it cannot naturally get — if it races with obvious reluctance from a midfield spot under Brian Hayes, it effectively removes a horse with a 1W1P similar-going record from the competitive picture.
Written In My Soul has pulled up in two of its last three starts; watch for early signs of labouring that could bring the field to a halt unexpectedly or cause interference at a hurdle.

The pace band is entirely dependent on Lemmy Caution's front-running — if Playtime is sent forward aggressively by Kennedy to test the leader, the race shape could shift sharply towards a more contested early gallop that benefits hold-up types like Gangster Granny.

Gangster Granny is the only runner with multiple wins specifically at 2m6f on good ground; if the race is run at a genuine clip rather than a crawl, its finishing profile becomes considerably more relevant.

races.name: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner, 10 days since last run is sharp enough, visor and hood in headgear, good-going form solid across 15 comparable runs but at OR 111 he is top-rated and will have rivals at his heels throughout; STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence if he is squeezed off the front.

runners_data.name: Nakassama
runners_data.note: Good-ground specialist with two wins and three placings from 10 comparable runs, 16 days since last outing is fine, hold-up style means he needs the pace to be genuine but he has proven closing ability over this trip at similar trips.

runners_data.name: Ringdufferin
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type whose recent form figures include a couple of blanks, 31 days off may have freshened him, good-ground record is solid but his best figures came at shorter trips and the 2m6f test here is near his ceiling.

runners_data.name: Typical Thomas
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up horse, 18 days since last run, good-ground performer with 13 qualifying runs in similar conditions yielding two wins and three places — the experience advantage in a big field is real, though a 7lb claimer (Smithers) rides.

runners_data.name: Cozone
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with a win and two places from seven good-ground qualifying runs; Keith Donoghue is an experienced partner and the 31-day break follows a third-place effort, making this an interesting return, though this is a stiffer trip than his best recent efforts.

runners_data.name: Ivybrook
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 198 days off, no wins and just one place from five good-ground runs — the layoff is the dominant concern here and he would need to bounce back close to his best to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Andys Flame
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with strong stamina profile, headgear includes tongue-tie and visor, 31 days since last run at OR 105, won over 2m4f on good ground last season and the step up to 2m6f could suit; trainer McConnell has been firing blanks recently (0/48 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Joya Del Mar
runners_data.note: Prominent-style horse with two wins from 11 good-ground comparable runs, consistent placing record, 31-day break is standard, headgear (hood/tongue-tie) worn; races for the McLoughlin yard whose 14-day figures are quiet but Joya Del Mar's own form is the story.

runners_data.name: Tribal Moon
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent type, lightly raced in comparable conditions (5/15 qualifying runs), only one place on good ground, 18 days since last run — young and unexposed, which is both the appeal and the risk in a competitive 18-runner handicap.

runners_data.name: Eastern Wind
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse pushed to a midfield mapping because the rear is overcrowded — his last five runs are all at shorter trips (10-17f) than today's 2m6f, raising a clear stamina question, and the STYLE_FIT tag means his position may not reflect his true race role.

runners_data.name: Oh Janey
runners_data.note: Hold-up type, 61 days between runs is the longest break in the field, won over 2m2f on good ground (18f) and has placed twice in similar conditions — the fitness query is real but she has good-ground ability if cherry-ripe.

runners_data.name: Morell River
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with two wins from nine good-ground qualifying runs, Colin Bowe yard is 1/1 in 14 days, 37-day break standard, consistent recent placing record at around this trip — one of the more solid profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Adaliz
runners_data.note: Prominent type trained by De Bromhead (5/38 in 14 days — active yard), two wins at this trip on good ground, 37-day break, OR 101 gives weight relief over the top-rated runners; strong claims for any scenario that rewards prominent-style runners.

runners_data.name: Boston Beach
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse mapped to midfield because the rear is congested — the more pressing issue is 576 days off the track, form string shows no wins or places in four career runs on good ground, and Gordon Elliott entry provides some hope but the fitness risk is enormous.

runners_data.name: Caher Roes Den
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained hold-up horse placed to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear; 455-day absence is a serious concern, best form came on soft ground (three places at 24f soft), and the good ground here is not where he has shown his best.

runners_data.name: Mickey Cohen
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer whose position on the map understates his likely early role — placed to midfield because there are more prominent types than can sit there; Noel Meade sends him just two days after a run, which is a red flag unless a Reserve slot means this is a placeholder entry.

runners_data.name: Fabhcun
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse represented on the map in midfield due to rear overcrowding; form figures show two pulled-ups and a sixth in five recent runs, no wins or places from qualifying conditions, and Elliott's 10/63 14-day strike rate is for the yard not this horse specifically — modest claims.

runners_data.name: Tolka Row
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer who cannot get his preferred spot given the volume of similar-style runners — mapped to midfield as a result; 10 days since last run, no wins from four good-ground runs, and the Reserve jockey tag adds uncertainty about who actually rides.

races.paceDynamic: Mephisto is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push him, should control from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over 2m6f on good ground. However, this is a field saturated with prominent-leaning types — Cozone, Ivybrook, Joya Del Mar, Tribal Moon, Morell River and Adaliz all want to race close to the pace, meaning the early sections will be more competitive than the single front-runner label implies. Mickey Cohen and Tolka Row are natural prominent racers who have been mapped to midfield because there simply is not room for all of them to sit where they want; Cozone, Joya Del Mar and Morell River are most likely to successfully enforce their natural position behind Mephisto. A contested but not truly fast tempo over this trip on good ground sets up a race where horses that can travel prominently and sustain their effort from three out will be at an advantage — closers reliant on a true end-to-end gallop are less well served, as the pace, while not soft, is unlikely to be severe enough to produce a mass collapse at the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mephisto Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Mephisto travels comfortably in front and the field streams out behind at a fair but unforced pace, allowing the prominent holders to chase home.
scenarios.body: Mephisto sets a rhythm that suits those just behind him, and horses like Cozone, Joya Del Mar and Morell River — all with strong good-ground form at this trip — track him into contention and hit the line hardest; the hold-up brigade never gets the pace injection it needs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types crowd the early pace and the gallop becomes ragged, leaving hold-up horses within striking range to pounce late.
scenarios.body: A bunch finish develops in the straight with fresher hold-up types emerging from mid-pack; horses like Nakassama, Oh Janey and Typical Thomas, who have been quietly switched off, get first run on rivals who have emptied.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Slog, Stayer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the 18-runner field creates a genuine end-to-end gallop and the trip truly tests stamina in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a test of pure stamina and horses with the deepest form at 2m6f and proven good-ground records — Morell River, Adaliz and Andys Flame — come through beaten rivals to dominate late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Outsider Ambushes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent types — Mickey Cohen or Tolka Row — manages to secure a better early position than expected and is never challenged for their slot.
scenarios.body: Racing fresher than rivals who have scrapped for position from early, a well-handicapped prominent type slips clear from two out with nothing able to mount a challenge; Mickey Cohen's youth and hurdles form make him the likelier vehicle.

watchPoints.text: Mickey Cohen is flagged as just 2 days since his last run — if this is a genuine entry rather than a reserve placeholder, confirm the jockey (Reserve 1) before the race as the combination has significant bearing on his chance.

Caher Roes Den and Boston Beach are both returning from 455 and 576 days off respectively — in an 18-runner handicap, blundering, stopping or falling rivals rounding the final turn could cause traffic problems even for horses not directly involved.

The cluster of prominent types — Cozone, Joya Del Mar, Morell River, Tribal Moon and Adaliz — will jostle for the four or five positions immediately behind Mephisto; watch the early pace in the first mile, as any scrimmaging could unbalance hold-up horses trying to settle at the back.

Tolka Row and Mickey Cohen, both natural prominent runners mapped to midfield, could push forward from their drawn positions and inject unexpected pace into the race if their jockeys (all Reserve riders) try to reclaim their natural spot.

Ivybrook has not run in 198 days for a yard (McLoughlin) that also runs Joya Del Mar — watch how Ivybrook travels in the early stages as a fitness gauge; if he struggles to hold his position, it confirms the likely pace shape and the strength of the prominent contest ahead of him.
